gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the BLUETTI Elite 400 (3,840 Wh rated) delivered on a meter: 3.07 kWh at StorageReview (2026-11-02) and about 3,130 Wh at Notebookcheck (250 W load), which is 80-82% of rated, against the 3,790 Wh (92.5%) OutdoorGearLab measured from the 4,096 Wh EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages and two more StormWatts results, all opened 2026-11-18. PowerSized's DELTA Pro 3 review (cited) already carries OutdoorGearLab's 3,790 Wh / 93% and 1,293 Wh per hour charge figures, so the DELTA Pro 3 half is not new. StormWatts' solar-input comparison and bundle-vs-separate pages (both cited) and its kits-at-same-panel-watts and flagships pages each say they did no testing and carry no named third-party measurement; they use an assumed 0.85 efficiency. None of the five mentions the Elite 400. No page puts measured delivered Wh side by side for the 4 kWh class, and none has the idle-draw figures (Elite 400 about 20 W, HomePower 3600 Plus about 34 W, both The Solar Lab). Not checked: solargenadvisor.com and theoutageplan.com failed to open (certificate error), and energysage, solargenreview, storedenergylab, outagereadyhq, pluginsolarcheck, theoutageready, practicalbuyerguide and staypoweredhq were not opened within the call budget.
decides: It confirms the value ranking and corrects the size claim; it does not flip the pick. The Elite 400 kits are within 256 Wh of the DELTA Pro 3 on the label, but about 660-720 Wh behind on a meter (different testers and loads, so indicative only). At the link price the Elite 400 + 350 W kit is $1,756.55 / 3,070 Wh = $0.57 per measured Wh, against $0.46 per rated Wh. The DELTA Pro 3 + 400 W kit at the $3,099 StormWatts read on 2026-10-16 would be $0.82 per measured Wh, so the Elite 400 stays the cheaper kit per delivered Wh. Notebookcheck saw the Elite 400's efficiency rise to about 93% at 1,800 W, so the shortfall applies to light loads such as a fridge or router, which fits The Solar Lab's 20 W inverter idle draw. The Elite 400 kits are pre-orders (mid to late January 2027 per the kit table), so they belong as the cheaper option for a shopper who can wait, with the delivered-Wh caveat in the row. The ship-now ALLPOWERS R3500 kits have no named delivered-Wh measurement, so their rows must use rated Wh and say so. PowerSized reported EcoFlow's DELTA Pro 3 solar kits out of stock on 2026-11-17, so that row's shipping state needs today's check.

findings.label: Delivered AC energy on a full discharge (StorageReview)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 400 Review: 3840Wh, 2600W, 6ms UPS switchover on wheels (StorageReview, Dylan Bryan, 2026-11-02)
findings.note: Method: a blower fan as a steady inductive load with a power meter in line, run until shutdown. StorageReview's own comparison: 80% on the Elite 400 against 89% on the Elite 300 and 92% on the Elite 200 V2. Arithmetic: 3,070 / 3,840 = 79.9%.

findings.label: Delivered AC energy at about 250 W (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about 3,130 Wh, just under 82% of rated
findings.source_title: Lighter than the competition: Bluetti Elite 400 XXL powerstation review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2026-04-11, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Continuous AC draw of about 250 W. Notebookcheck tested the EU version and says it differs from the US version. Arithmetic: 3,130 / 3,840 = 81.5%.

findings.label: Efficiency at a heavy load (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: Lighter than the competition: Bluetti Elite 400 XXL powerstation review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: EU version. Notebookcheck says that at the 250 W load it lags behind the Elite 300 and some competitors. The 80-82% figure therefore applies to light loads.

findings.label: Wall energy for a 0-100% charge and round trip
findings.value: 3.96 kWh from the wall, round trip near 78% (StorageReview); just under 4,400 Wh in fast mode (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: StorageReview: 3.07 / 3.96 = 77.5%. The Notebookcheck figure is from its review (URL in the rows above), EU version, 2,300 W fast mode, where it says about 87% reached the battery. My arithmetic for Notebookcheck: 3,130 / 4,400 = 71% round trip at the 250 W load.

findings.label: AC inverter idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 400 Review: A Strange Unit That Could Be Genius (The Solar Lab, © 2026, no byline or date on the page)
findings.note: The Solar Lab says the unit could sit powered on for almost 8 days before draining. Arithmetic: 3,840 Wh / 20 W = 192 h = 8.0 days. It also measured 'efficiency at right around 77%' without saying whether that is inverter-only or round trip, and a 0-100% AC charge in 2 h 27 min at 1,800 W input.

findings.label: Fan noise (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: Lighter than the competition: Bluetti Elite 400 XXL powerstation review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: EU version, measured from one metre.

findings.label: UPS switchover (StorageReview)
findings.value: 6 ms to battery, 14.8 ms back to utility
findings.note: 740 W Dell workstation load, Quarch capture. BLUETTI's advertised rating is 15 ms.

findings.label: Kit price per measured Wh (arithmetic)
findings.note: Link prices from the 'Kits we link' table (read 2026-11-17): $1,756.55, $1,804.05, $2,136.55 and $2,325.60, each divided by StorageReview's 3,070 Wh. On the 3,840 Wh rating the first two are $0.46 and $0.47. All four kits are pre-orders in that table.

findings.label: Delivered energy on a full charge (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 Review (GearLab, Kenji Mowrey, 2026-01-13)
findings.note: Measured on GearLab's test jig. The text says 'over 93%'; 3,790 / 4,096 = 92.5%. Also measured: 1,293 Wh per hour average charge from a 120 V outlet, and 114.1 lb. No dB figure. PowerSized (cited by ChatGPT) already quotes this figure.

findings.label: Average discharge across several cycles (Digital Trends)
findings.value: 3.7 kWh; close to 5 kWh from the wall for a 0-100% charge
findings.source_title: This brute of a power station will power almost anything, even A/C (Digital Trends, Simon Sage, 2024-06-25)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 3,700 / 4,096 = 90%; 3.7 / 5 = about 74% round trip. The 0-100% charge took about three hours. The sub-40 dB noise figure in the article is EcoFlow's claim, not a measurement.

findings.label: Measured delivered Wh side by side, 4 kWh class
findings.value: DELTA Pro 3: 3,790 Wh (92.5%); Elite 400: 3,070-3,130 Wh (80-82%); the gap is 660-720 Wh against 256 Wh on the label
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 Review (GearLab) with StorageReview and Notebookcheck Elite 400 reviews
findings.note: Arithmetic: 3,790 − 3,070 = 720; 3,790 − 3,130 = 660; 4,096 − 3,840 = 256. Three testers, three loads, not one method, so the page should label it indicative. At the $3,099 StormWatts read for the DELTA Pro 3 + 400 W kit on 2026-10-16 (not re-read today), 3,099 / 3,790 = $0.82 per measured Wh.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX F3800 (original, not the Plus)
findings.label: Usable capacity after a 100% charge (StorageReview)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800: Do We Really Need Gas Generators? (StorageReview, Kevin OBrien, 2024-06-21)
findings.note: This is the 2024 F3800, with the same 3,840 Wh rating as the F3800 Plus; it is not a test of the Plus. Arithmetic: 2,980 / 3,840 = 77.6%; 2,980 / 4,930 = 60%. The load is not stated.

findings.label: Inverter efficiency, idle draw and surge (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 89% inverter efficiency; idle about 34 W; surged to 5,900 W without tripping
findings.source_title: Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus review (The Solar Lab, © 2026, no byline or date on the page)
findings.note: The page writes the idle figure as '34 watts per hour'. Arithmetic: 3,584 Wh / 34 W = 105 h, about 4.4 days with the inverter on and no load. Also: about 2.5 hours from a wall outlet, and about 4 hours to full from a 1,000 W solar array in clear conditions. The same page cites 91% for the Anker F3800 Plus as a comparison, without showing that test.

findings.label: Measured charge and solar input (BatterySkills)
findings.value: 0-100% in 2 h 15 min at a steady 1,550 W from a 20 A outlet; 780 W peak from two 400 W panels in series
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS R3500 2-Hour Charge Review (BatterySkills, Bernard Ryan, 2025-09-16)
findings.note: The page names no meter and its runtime table is labelled 'Estimated', so treat it as weak. 780 / 800 = 97.5% of panel rating, which is high next to the 85% pv magazine saw on Anker panels. It also reports starting a well pump with a 3,800 W surge and a 20 ms UPS switchover. No delivered-Wh figure.

findings.label: Delivered energy, idle draw and panel output (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA / ESS News)
findings.value: 4.87 kWh app-reported (97% of 5,024 Wh); about 10 W idle with 120 V output on; 680 W peak from 2× PS400 (85% of 800 W); 6.24 kWh from the wall, 78% round trip
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review: 5 kWh on wheels, tested through a real power outage (pv magazine USA, Andrew Riha, 2026-10-28; read on the Now.Solar repost)
findings.note: At 5,024 Wh this is 25.6% over 4,000 Wh, outside the roughly 20% size line, so it is context only. The delivered figure comes from Anker's app, not an external meter. Idle is from 5% lost in 24 hours. The 680 W reading was on a sunny October day in Northern California on a pre-release unit, with the same panel pair as the S5000 + 2× 400 W kit we link. I read the repost, not the pv magazine page itself.

findings.label: What the rivals use in place of a measurement
findings.value: an assumed 0.85 charge-path efficiency (StormWatts) and an assumed 85% usable capacity (PowerSized's runtime table)
findings.source_title: 5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input (StormWatts, 2026-11-16)
findings.note: StormWatts states 'We haven't tested any of these four stations.' PowerSized (https://powersized.com/reviews/ecoflow-delta-pro-3/, read 2026-11-18) says it has not tested the unit and relies on OutdoorGearLab. The measured range across these units is 78-97%, so a flat 85% overstates the Elite 400 and understates the DELTA Pro 3.

unsourced: Delivered Wh for the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus itself: pcmag.com could not be fetched; a search result showed a repost quoting about 4,248 Wh, apparently with an expansion battery attached, which I did not open or verify. Only StorageReview's 2024 test of the original F3800 is sourced.
Delivered Wh for the Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus: The Solar Lab gives inverter efficiency and idle draw but no discharge total; no other named tester found.

Measured idle draw for the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 and Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus: not in any review opened.

Whether StorageReview tested the US version of the Elite 400: not stated in what I read; Notebookcheck's unit was the EU version.
